sections.heading: Fiji anchored to bottom of Nations Championship table after 11-try England rout
sections.body: Fiji remain 12th of 12 in the Nations Championship log following three consecutive defeats, carrying a tournament-worst points difference of -96. The scale of the struggle was highlighted by an 8-73 loss to England, a result the BBC described as a thrashing of a "sorry" Fijian side. Replacement Henry Pollock scored a second-half hat-trick as England crossed for 11 tries to end their own five-Test losing streak. Following a 17-33 defeat to Scotland in Round 3, Fiji face France next.

lead.why: Fiji's winless Nations Championship start and the defensive frailties exposed in the England rout remain the most significant story for the senior men's side.

sections.heading: Tevita Tuiloa launches Fiji Sevens collectable range to honour memorable moments
sections.body: Fiji Rugby and Coca-Cola Europacific Partners have launched a series of limited-edition cans and bottles featuring the men’s Sevens side. The collection celebrates eight specific highlights from the 2025 Hong Kong and Singapore tournaments. At a launch event in Suva, Commercial Director Tevita Tuiloa stated that "Fiji’s rugby story belongs to all of us" as the union looks to inspire young players. The Flying Fijians currently sit bottom of the Nations Championship table following their 17-33 loss to Scotland.

sections.heading: Joe Carpenter eyes England return by outshining rival George Furbank
sections.body: Sale full-back Joe Carpenter is targeting a standout performance in Sunday’s Premiership clash against Harlequins to bolster his England selection prospects. After benefitting from a full pre-season, Carpenter has been in prolific form, ranking among the league's top defenders beaten. With George Furbank currently occupying the England full-back role, Carpenter admits he is motivated by the direct competition. “It would be nice to have a very good performance against them and against that England competition,” Carpenter said.

sections.heading: England's Twickenham finals quota raised as Springboks and All Blacks sell out
sections.body: England's home allocation for the Nations Championship finals weekend at Twickenham has been lifted from 1,500 to 2,000 tickets to meet early demand, according to the Guardian. South Africa and New Zealand have already sold out their own 1,000-ticket 'Support your team' allocations, and 60-65% of finals-weekend tickets are gone overall. Tickets for England were still on sale at £164.80 on Wednesday, with England supporters making up the bulk of sales across the pool stages and the finals.

sections.heading: NBA Star Victor Wembanyama Completes Training Stint With Provence Rugby
sections.body: NBA superstar Victor Wembanyama has completed a training stint with French second-tier side Provence, citing the squad's camaraderie as a major inspiration. The 22-year-old Spurs forward participated in line-out drills, tackling practice, and conditioning sessions alongside the professional squad during his summer off-season. Wembanyama, who previously sought strength training with Shaolin monks, praised the club's environment, stating, "The training was really hard, really good for stability, movement patterns and developing strength, but I am more grateful for the experience."

sections.heading: France’s 1977 Grand Slam side remembered for its enduring impact
sections.body: The 1977 French side remains a benchmark for inspiration in international rugby, noted for a squad that commanded respect before a ball was even kicked. Featuring a legendary back row of Jean-Pierre Rives and Jean-Claude Skrela, the team’s Five Nations Grand Slam victory continues to define a specific era of French flair. Alongside iconic international outfits like the All Blacks, that 1977 cohort is frequently cited as a side that transcends mere statistics to capture the imagination of fans.

lead.why: This story contextualises the 1977 Grand Slam side's legacy within the broader history of inspiring teams.

sections.heading: Italy prepare for South Africa return to the Allianz Stadium
sections.body: Top-level international rugby returns to Turin as Italy host reigning world champions South Africa at the Allianz Stadium. sections.heading: Edinburgh scrum-half Hector Patterson weighs potential switch to represent England
sections.body: Edinburgh’s Hector Patterson is attracting interest from English clubs as he nears the end of his current contract, raising questions about his long-term international future. While the 21-year-old represented Scotland at U18 and U20 levels, helping them to the 2024 World Rugby U20 Trophy, his grandparental eligibility leaves the door open for an England call-up. With Bath reportedly monitoring his situation, his next career move could prove pivotal before he is capped at senior level by Scotland.

sections.heading: Felipe Contepomi confirms Shaun Edwards and Mario Ledesma as assistants
sections.body: Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi has secured two major appointments to his backroom staff, with Shaun Edwards and Mario Ledesma signing on through to the 2027 Rugby World Cup. Edwards, who is currently working with the Red Roses, will join as defence coach, while former Pumas head coach Ledesma returns to lead the forwards. Contepomi noted, "Mario and Shaun arrive at Los Pumas with enormous international experience." The duo will begin their roles at the end of October.

Ledesma, the former Pumas head coach, returns as forwards coach, while Edwards takes the lead on defence after concluding his consultancy with the Red Roses. Contepomi noted that both men "arrive at Los Pumas with enormous international experience" and will be instrumental in preparing the side for upcoming Nations Championship fixtures against Ireland, Italy, and France.

sections.heading: Les Kiss backs Wallabies to return fire in Sydney rematch
sections.body: Wallabies head coach Les Kiss has urged his side to respond following a heavy 50-19 defeat to the All Blacks at Eden Park. The result marked Australia’s first loss under his tenure, snapping a five-match unbeaten run. Kiss remains confident in his squad's underlying culture despite the setback. "You get a knockback, you find out more about yourself and that’s what we’ll do," said Kiss, who is now prioritising technical adjustments in order to "turn the dial" for next Saturday's clash.

The victory marks a successful return to the top of the podium for the Japanese women, who last won the title two Games ago. Across the tournament, Japan showed consistency, maintaining their competitive edge throughout the final day to clinch the gold in a hard-fought contest against their closest regional rivals.

sections.heading: New Zealand thrash Australia 50-19 to retain the Bledisloe Cup
sections.body: New Zealand secured the Bledisloe Cup with a comprehensive 50-19 victory over the Wallabies at Eden Park. After a competitive first half, the All Blacks surged away to score five second-half tries, extending their unbeaten streak at the venue to 54 matches. Despite the win, Dave Rennie faces fresh injury concerns: Scott Barrett failed an HIA, Leroy Carter suffered an ankle injury after scoring, and Anton Segner departed with a head wound. Rennie noted, "We just lost key moments in Africa, and we won a lot of those tonight."

sections.body: The Springboks remain top of World Rugby's men's rankings, but New Zealand's 50-19 win over Australia in the first Bledisloe Cup Test at Eden Park has narrowed the gap sharply. The All Blacks gained 0.66 points to reach 91.81, leaving South Africa on 93.09, just 1.28 clear.
